title: Integrated Analysis of p53 Immunohistochemical Expression and TP53 Sequencing for Prognostic Assessment of Triple Negative Breast Cancer After Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy
content: Background: The prognostic significance of p53 immunohistochemical expression in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remains controversial, particularly following neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC). Whether integrating p53 immunohistochemistry with TP53 mutational analysis provides additional prognostic information has not been fully established. This study evaluated the relationship between p53 expression, TP53 mutational profiles, longitudinal TP53 dynamics, and clinical outcome in patients with TNBC treated with NAC. Methods: Forty-three patients with stage I–III TNBC treated with NAC were retrospectively analyzed. p53 immunohistochemistry performed on tumor samples collected before NAC was evaluated using binary (< 10% vs. ≥10%) and three-tier (< 10%, 10–50%, >50%) classifications. Targeted sequencing was performed on tumors before treatment and available matched post-treatment samples to characterize TP53 variants and longitudinal mutational dynamics. Associations with pathological complete response (pCR), recurrence, disease-free survival (DFS), and overall survival (OS) were assessed. Results: High p53 expression assessed before NAC(≥10%) was significantly associated with improved DFS and OS among patients achieving pCR, whereas no significant prognostic association was observed in patients with residual disease. TP53 was the most frequently altered gene and exhibited substantial inter-patient heterogeneity in variant number and allele frequency. Longitudinal analysis demonstrated both persistence and remodeling of TP53 variants following NAC, with distinct evolutionary patterns across clinical outcome groups. The prognostic value of p53 immunohistochemical expression differed according to treatment response, while longitudinal TP53 sequencing revealed dynamic clonal remodeling following neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Conclusions: Combined assessment of p53 immunohistochemical expression and TP53 mutational profiling offers complementary prognostic information in TNBC treated with NAC. Integrating routine pathology with molecular analysis may improve risk stratification and provides insight into treatment-associated TP53 clonal evolution.
